extracted.intended_audience: early-career scientists (untenured faculty and DOE lab/user-facility staff), research administrators preparing grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Announcement and application requirements for the U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science Early Career Research Program (FY2025), describing who is eligible, eligible program offices, funding levels and durations, and key deadlines and submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant position eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for the program, a researcher must be an untenured, tenure-track assistant or associate professor at a U.S. academic institution or a full-time employee at a DOE national laboratory or Office of Science user facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording emphasizes untenured, tenure-track assistant or associate professors at U.S. academic institutions, and full-time employees at DOE national laboratories or Office of Science user facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctorate timeframe eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be within 10 years of having earned their doctorate degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 10-year post-doctorate limit is stated as an eligibility requirement; the announcement does not provide exceptions or extensions in the text shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible institutions and workplaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards may be to U.S. academic institutions, DOE national laboratories, and Office of Science user facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement distinguishes awards made to institutions of higher education versus DOE national laboratories/user facilities (see funding amounts entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amounts and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards to an institution of higher education will be approximately $875,000 over five years and awards to a DOE national laboratory or Office of Science user facility will be approximately $2,750,000 over five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duration for both types is five years; amounts are approximate and differ by recipient type (institution vs national lab/user facility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of awards / program scale
rubrics_metrics.description: The program will support over 80 early career researchers for five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates scale of the FY2025 competition (over 80 awards expected).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible Office of Science program offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Early career researchers may apply to one of eight Office of Science program offices: Advanced Scientific Computing Research; Biological and Environmental Research; Basic Energy Sciences; Fusion Energy Sciences; High Energy Physics; Nuclear Physics; Accelerator R&D and Production; and Isotope R&D and Production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must choose one of these eight program offices when applying; proposed research should align with the chosen office's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research topic fit to programmatic priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed research topics must fall within the programmatic priorities of DOE’s Office of Science, which are provided in the program announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the program announcement for the detailed programmatic priorities; topic fit is a prerequisite for eligibility/consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection/funding mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding will be competitively awarded on the basis of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are merit-based and subject to peer review; the announcement does not list specific review criteria on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application requirement and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-applications are mandatory and are due on February 18, 2025, at 5:00 p.m. ET.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-application submission is required; failure to submit a pre-application by the deadline would likely disqualify candidates from moving forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full application invitation and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Only those applicants that receive notification from DOE encouraging a formal application may submit full applications. Applications will be due on April 22, 2025, at 11:59 p.m. ET.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full applications are by invitation only (i.e., only pre-applicants who are encouraged may submit). Note the strict full application deadline/time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informational webinar
rubrics_metrics.description: A webinar on this opportunity will be held on January 31, 2025, at 4:00 p.m. ET.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement provides a registration link for the webinar; attending or reviewing webinar materials may help applicants understand priorities and process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find further information
rubrics_metrics.description: Further information can be found on the Office of Science funding opportunities page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are directed to the program announcement and funding opportunities page for full details, programmatic priorities, application instructions, and possibly review criteria and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose / evaluation emphasis (promotional framing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The program supports the research of outstanding scientists early in their careers and 'allows them to pursue new ideas and harness the resources of the user facilities to increase the potential for breakthrough new discoveries.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While promotional, this language signals emphasis on innovative ideas, use of Office of Science user facilities, and potential for breakthrough discoveries — factors applicants should highlight in proposals, though formal review criteria are not enumerated on this page.
